title: 天仙子·水调数声持酒听
title_en: To the Tune Tian Xian Zi: A Few Notes of the Water Melody
author: 张先

form.en: ci lyric to the tune Tian Xian Zi, two stanzas

readings.zh: 这里是“曲调”的意思，读 diào。
这里是“几”的意思，读 shù。
现在读 tīng。这首词押仄声韵，“听”在古代也有去声的读法，和“醒、镜、影”押韵。
readings.en: Read tīng today. The lyric rhymes on oblique tones, and in old times this character also had a falling-tone reading, so it rhymed with xǐng, jìng and yǐng.

readings.zh: 这里是“记得、明白”的意思，读 xǐng，不读 shěng。
readings.en: Read xǐng here, meaning "to remember clearly", not shěng.

readings.zh: 这里是“一层又一层”的意思，读 chóng。
readings.en: Read chóng here, meaning "layer upon layer".

glosses.zh: 水调：一种曲调的名字，相传是隋炀帝时传下来的，声音很哀伤。
glosses.en: shuǐ diào: Water Melody: the name of a tune said to come from the time of Emperor Yang of Sui. It sounded sad.

glosses.zh: 数声：几声，这里指听了几段曲子。
glosses.en: shù shēng: a few notes, a few snatches of the song.
chí jiǔ: holding a cup of wine.

glosses.zh: 愁未醒：酒醒了，可心里的愁还没散。
glosses.en: chóu wèi xǐng: the sorrow has not worn off, though the wine has.

glosses.zh: 临晚镜：傍晚对着镜子照。
glosses.en: lín wǎn jìng: looking in the mirror in the evening.

glosses.zh: 伤：为……难过。流景：像流水一样过去的时光。
glosses.en: shāng liú jǐng: shāng means to grieve over; liú jǐng is time flowing away like water.
hòu qī: plans and promises for later.

glosses.zh: 空记省：白白地记得清清楚楚。空，白白地。
glosses.en: kōng jì xǐng: remembering clearly, but in vain.

glosses.zh: 并禽：成对的鸟，比如鸳鸯。
glosses.en: bìng qín: birds in pairs, such as mandarin ducks.

glosses.zh: 云破：云层裂开了一道缝。
glosses.en: yún pò: the clouds break open.

glosses.zh: 花弄影：花在风里摇动，好像在摆弄自己的影子。
glosses.en: huā nòng yǐng: the flowers sway as if playing with their own shadows.

glosses.zh: 帘幕：挂在门窗上的帘子和帷幕。
glosses.en: lián mù: curtains and hangings over doors and windows.

glosses.zh: 密遮灯：把灯光严严实实地遮住。
glosses.en: mì zhē dēng: closely shielding the lamp.

glosses.zh: 满径：铺满了小路。径，小路。
glosses.en: mǎn jìng: covering the path. Jìng is a small path.

translation.zh: 拿着酒杯，听了几段哀伤的《水调》，
translation.en: Cup in hand, I listen to a few notes of the sad Water Melody.

translation.zh: 中午喝醉了，醒来时酒醒了，愁却还没散。
translation.en: I wake from my noon drunkenness, but my sorrow does not wake away.

translation.zh: 送走了春天，春天什么时候才会再回来？
translation.en: I see spring off; when will spring come back?
In the evening I face the mirror,
grieving for the time that slips away.

translation.zh: 过去的事和以后的约定，我白白地记得清清楚楚。
translation.en: Past things and future promises, I remember them clearly, all for nothing.

translation.zh: 沙滩上成对的鸟儿依偎着，池塘上天色暗了下来。
translation.en: On the sand the paired birds settle; over the pond it grows dark.

translation.zh: 云层裂开，月亮出来了，花儿在月光下摇动着自己的影子。
translation.en: The clouds break, the moon comes out, and the flowers play with their shadows.

translation.zh: 一层层帘幕把灯光严严地遮住，
translation.en: Layer on layer of curtains closely shield the lamp,
the wind outside will not settle,
and people have just fallen quiet.

translation.zh: 明天，落下的花瓣应该会铺满小路吧。
translation.en: Tomorrow, fallen petals will surely cover the path.

background.zh: 张先原来在词题下写了一句话，说他当时在嘉禾（今浙江嘉兴）做“小倅”，也就是知州的副手，因为生病在家睡觉，没有去参加官府的宴会。一般认为这时他已经五十岁左右，一说是庆历元年（1041）前后。暮春时节，他一个人喝酒、听曲，看着春天走了，心里有说不出的愁，就写了这首词。
background.en: Under the title, Zhang Xian wrote a short note. He said he was then a deputy official in Jiahe, today's Jiaxing in Zhejiang. He was ill and lying at home, so he did not go to a banquet at the government office. He is usually thought to have been about fifty then; one view dates it to around 1041. It was late spring. Drinking alone and listening to music, he watched spring leave and felt a sadness he could not put into words, so he wrote this lyric.

author_note.zh: 张先（990—1078），字子野，乌程（今浙江湖州）人，北宋词人。他很会写“影”，自己最得意的三句里都有“影”字，人们就叫他“张三影”。“云破月来花弄影”就是其中最有名的一句。
author_note.en: Zhang Xian (990–1078), courtesy name Ziye, came from Wucheng, today's Huzhou in Zhejiang. He was a lyric poet of the Northern Song. He was very good at writing about shadows. His three favourite lines of his own all use the word for shadow, so people called him "Three-Shadows Zhang". "The clouds break, the moon comes out, and the flowers play with their shadows" is the most famous of them.

appreciation.zh: 上阕写愁。他听着哀伤的曲子喝酒，醉了又醒，愁却醒不了。春天走了，镜子里的自己也老了，过去的事、将来的约定都只能空想。下阕写夜景。天黑了，沙滩上的鸟儿成双成对，他却是一个人。忽然云开了，月亮出来，花在风里摇动，好像在和自己的影子玩。一个“弄”字，让花活了起来，静静的夜也有了动静。最后他放下帘子、遮住灯，听着风声想：明天小路上该落满花瓣了。这是在可惜春天，也是在可惜自己的年华。
appreciation.en: The first stanza is about sorrow. He drinks while listening to a sad tune. He gets drunk and wakes up, but the sorrow does not wake away. Spring is leaving, the face in the mirror is growing old, and past events and future promises are only empty thoughts. The second stanza is a night scene. It grows dark, and the birds on the sand are in pairs, while he is alone. Suddenly the clouds part, the moon comes out, and the flowers sway as if playing with their shadows. The single word "play" brings the flowers to life and puts movement into the quiet night. At the end he lowers the curtains and shields the lamp. Listening to the wind, he thinks: tomorrow the path will be covered in petals. He is sorry for spring, and sorry for his own passing years too.
